data.summary:
Input: A string s.
Output: The longest substring within s that reads the same forwards and backwards.
Rules: If there are multiple palindromes of the same maximum length, return any one of them.
constraints: s consists of only digits and English letters

data.generator_code:
import random

def generate(rng, n):
    alphabet = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789"
    s = "".join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))
    return [s]

def generate_worst(rng, n):
    s = "a" * n
    return [s]

data.key_insight: A palindrome mirrors around its center. There are 2n - 1 possible centers for a string of length n (each character and each space between characters). We can expand outwards from each center as long as the characters match to find the longest palindrome.

steps.title: Handle edge cases
steps.detail: If the string is empty or has length 1, return the string itself as it is already a palindrome.

steps.title: Iterate through all possible centers
steps.detail: For every index i in the string, consider two centers: a single character center at i, and a two-character center between i and i + 1.

steps.title: Expand and track maximum length
steps.detail: For each center, expand outwards while the left and right pointers are within bounds and the characters match. Keep track of the start index and maximum length found so far.

steps.title: Return the result
steps.detail: Extract and return the substring corresponding to the best start index and maximum length found.

data.pattern_summary: Expand Around Center is used when you need to find subarrays or substrings defined by symmetry. Instead of checking every possible start and end point independently, you anchor on potential centers and expand outward as long as the symmetry holds.

pattern_options.name: Expand Around Center
pattern_options.feedback: Correct. Palindromes are symmetrical, meaning they look the same expanding outward from a center point or pair of points.

pattern_options.name: Sliding Window
pattern_options.feedback: Incorrect. Sliding windows typically adjust boundaries based on a condition like sum or character frequency, but palindromic symmetry does not guarantee a predictable window shrink or expand rule.

pattern_options.name: Dynamic Programming
pattern_options.feedback: Incorrect while possible, it is overkill here. DP builds solutions from smaller substrings, but checking centers directly avoids storing a 2D table.

pattern_options.name: Binary Search
pattern_options.feedback: Incorrect. The length of the longest palindrome does not exhibit a monotonic property where you can rule out entire halves of search ranges easily.

signals.hint: Implies you are examining contiguous segments of the string.

signals.phrase: reads the same forwards and backwards
signals.hint: Defines a palindrome, which inherently possesses a center of symmetry.

data.brute_force_idea: Check every possible start index and end index combination to generate every possible substring, check if each one is a palindrome, and keep track of the longest one found.
data.brute_force_why: There are O(n²) possible substrings, and checking whether each substring of length k is a palindrome takes O(k) time, leading to cubic total time.
data.bottleneck: The code repeatedly checks if overlapping or entirely separate substrings are palindromes from scratch, re-scanning characters that were already verified inside smaller substrings.
bottleneck_hints: Look at how many times you check characters that overlap between different substrings.
If you know a smaller substring is a palindrome, do you need to re-check all its internal characters when evaluating a larger substring?
Think about what information you throw away every time you move to a new start and end index pair.

data.overview: The algorithm finds the longest palindromic substring by treating each character and each gap between characters as a potential center and expanding outwards as far as matching characters allow. It tracks the maximum length and start index to extract the final substring.
data.intuition: Imagine poking a hole in a string at every single possible center point and shining a light outwards in both directions simultaneously; the furthest distance the light reaches before characters mismatch tells you the size of that palindrome.

pitfalls: Forgetting to check both odd-length (single character center) and even-length (between characters) palindromes.
Off-by-one errors when calculating the new start index from the max length and center index.
Not handling edge cases like single character strings correctly.

events.label: Coach: why the complexity is what it is

data.insight: The brute force approach checks every possible substring from scratch, leading to redundant work. The optimized approach instead treats every index (and the space between indices) as a potential center of a palindrome, expanding outward until the characters no longer match. This removes the inner loop of checking every substring by stopping immediately when a mismatch occurs.

derivation.note: The loop runs for each character in the string s.
Expands outward from a single character center, bounded by the string length.
Expands outward from a two-character center, bounded by the string length.

data.time_summary: Lines 16 and 17 execute an expansion that takes up to O(n) steps inside a loop on line 15 that runs n times. Multiplying the outer loop by the inner expansion cost yields O(n^2) total time.
data.space_summary: The algorithm only uses a few scalar variables (start, max_len, left, right) to track pointers, requiring O(1) auxiliary space.
data.takeaway: When a problem asks for substrings or subarrays defined by a symmetric property, consider centering at every possible pivot and expanding outward rather than generating all intervals.
mistakes: Forgetting to check both single-character centers (odd-length palindromes) and dual-character centers (even-length palindromes).
Miscalculating the starting index of the palindrome when extracting the substring using s[start:start + max_len].
Failing to handle edge cases like an empty string or a string of length 1.
